function: Channel estimation of the full time-frequency-space MIMO-OFDM channel tensor from pilot-position observations with a VAE generator trained adversarially (pp. 8-9).
system: Uplink MIMO-OFDM, UT with 2 antennas, BS with 4 (other setups up to 4x4), cross-polarized, 2.6 GHz, 15 kHz spacing, no RIS (pp. 3, 12).
method: VAE generator (VAENet) with CNN critic; Wasserstein-GAN gradient-penalty training plus reconstruction, KL and skewness losses on true channels (supervised), trained offline (pp. 9-11).
data_channel: Sionna CDL-B (3GPP TR 38.901) NLOS: 20,000 training, 10,000 test samples; second test set of ray-tracing (RT) channels of a Polytechnique Montreal scene (pp. 11-12, Table I).
test_conditions: Trained on CDL-B data (Table I); tested on CDL-B with varied speed, rays, clusters and on an unseen Polytechnique Montreal RT set at 50 m/s (pp. 12-14).
baselines: Non-learned only: LS with nearest-neighbour, linear and LMMSE interpolation (t-f, t-f-s, s-t-f orders); unscaled VAENet is a variant; no earlier learned estimator compared (pp. 7, 13).
metrics: NMSE, SSIM and BER (after LDPC decoding) versus SNR; inference time; FLOPs and parameters (pp. 11-14).
complexity: Big-O order O(N_ut K_ut,ant N_bs K_bs,ant N_sym N_sub); runtime in Table II (0.0545 s vs 0.66 s for LS+LMMSE); FLOPs and parameters in Fig. 6a (pp. 6, 12).
q1_support: p. 11: "the CDL-B channel model is generated using the CDL implementation provided in the Sionna library"; the CDL model is part of 3GPP TR 38.901 (p. 1).
q2_support: p. 14: "To fairly evaluate generalization, we tested the trained" VAENet on the Polytechnique Montreal ray-tracing set, unseen in training (Fig. 11b, Table III).
q3_support: p. 13: "the performance of the VAENet model is compared with conventional methods, specifically the LS channel estimator combined with interpolation techniques". Missing: no earlier learned estimator (DNN, GAN or VAE of refs. 12-14) in the results.
q4_support: p. 12: "the runtime of the end-to-end pipeline for each approach is measured on our device (MacBook M1)"; Big-O order of VAENet also given in Section V-E.
q5_support: p. 2: "The source code of this paper is available at https://github.com/TND-Lab/" High-Dimensional-MIMO-OFDM-Channel-Estimation (footnote 1).
notes: Included, area 2: learned VAE-GAN channel estimator. q1 rests on the Sionna CDL-B implementation of 3GPP TR 38.901. q2 rests on the Polytechnique Montreal RT test set (p. 14). q3 is 0: the only comparators are LS with interpolation and the unscaled variant of VAENet. LS+LMMSE (T-F-S) gets the best BER in Table III (p. 14), a mixed result. The training range of the geometry parameters is not clearly stated.
